ai.title: Catch analytics flush errors
ai.summary: Wraps `client.flush()` in try/catch within `flushAnalytics` to prevent unhandled promise rejections. Catches errors and logs them via `trackEvent` using new `AnalyticsEvent.FLUSH_FAILED` constant. Affects `common/src/analytics.ts` and `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`.

eli5.text: When the app tries to save your usage data and that save fails, it now quietly records the failure for the team instead of letting it crash the app. You won't see any difference in daily use, but behind the scenes the app stops treating a failed save as a fatal error. Engineers now get a signal when saves fail so they can investigate quietly.

ai.title: Reword edit snippet instructions using relace example
ai.summary: Updated `write_file` tool instructions in `backend/src/tools.ts` to prioritize `str_replace` for most edits. The prompt now explicitly defines an "Edit Snippet" format, requiring placeholder comments for unchanged regions and strict indentation preservation. A new "Optimizations" section warns that tool runtime scales with text volume, reinforcing minimal output.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a file but not rewrite the whole thing from scratch, the instructions it follows tell it to describe only the changes (using placeholder comments for the unchanged parts) and to keep the exact original indentation, rather than pasting large blocks of code that stay the same. This applies to anyone who triggers a partial file edit through the assistant's file-editing action today.

ai.title: Revert selective cachecontrol retention in messages.ts
ai.summary: Reverts logic that preserved `cache_control` on the last cached message, restoring behavior to strip `cache_control` from all messages in `getMessagesSubset`. This change simplifies `backend/src/util/messages.ts` by removing the loop identifying the last cached index. The scope is limited to the backend message utility, ensuring consistent cache header removal for subset generation.

eli5.text: Backend message handling no longer keeps cache settings on the final cached message; instead, it clears cache data from every message when building a shortened message list. Anyone relying on that special last-message retention will see it gone, while the rest experience consistent cleanup. This is in place now as a stability/maintenance change, not a visible behavior update.

ai.title: Fix truncateStringWithMessage formatting
ai.summary: Updated `truncateStringWithMessage` in `common/src/util/string.ts`. Default message changed from `TRUNCATED_DUE_TO_LENGTH` to `TRUNCATED DUE TO LENGTH`. Suffix/prefix formats adjusted for `END` and `START` modes to correctly position ellipses and slice string.

eli5.text: When long messages get shortened so they fit, the system now shows the truncation notice in a cleaner layout, placing the ellipsis inside the brackets and reading 'TRUNCATED DUE TO LENGTH' with spaces instead of underscores. If you scroll to where a long block of text is cut off, you will see the notice formatted consistently whether the text is trimmed from the end or the beginning. This fix applies to messages that exceed the length limit, so the notice looks tidy and predictable whenever truncation occurs.

eli5.text: The team added a new automated check that makes sure the assistant keeps producing the main response people expect when they ask it something. This check lives behind the scenes and runs on its own, so if someone accidentally breaks how the main answer is built, the system will catch it right away instead of letting it slip through. The change also updates the internal notes so developers know the check has to be run from a specific folder to pick up the right settings. If you looked, you would see a new file of automated tests and a small note in the documentation, no new buttons or features for you to click, just a safety net for the developers.

ai.title: Fix start truncation slice offset
ai.summary: Corrects off-by-one error in `truncateStringWithMessage` when `remove === 'START'`. Previously sliced from `maxLength - prefix.length`, now uses `str.length - maxLength + prefix.length` to properly account for prefix length. Internal fix in `common/src/util/string.ts`.

eli5.text: When an assistant replies are cut down to fit a smaller box and the cut happens at the beginning, the start of the remaining text was being trimmed by one character too many, so the last letter of the message got chopped off. The fix now keeps the correct amount so the full message is preserved when space is limited.

eli5.text: When the assistant is using tools and the system reaches the end of a response before a tool tag has been properly closed, the program now quietly adds the closing tag and continues, rather than raising a loud warning. This is an internal adjustment to how log messages are classified, so most people won't see a difference in their conversations.

ai.title: Refactor help menu layout and add example prompts
ai.summary: Simplified CLI help menu rendering in npm-app/src/menu.ts by removing conditional layout logic and replacing random color generation with fixed picocolors functions. Added new 'EXAMPLE PROMPTS' section and explicit 'codebuff --lite' / 'codebuff --max' mode commands to the command list. Included a warning note that Codebuff does not read .gitignore files.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant in a terminal, the startup menu now shows a fixed, stable set of colors instead of random ones, a new section called EXAMPLE PROMPTS with ready-to-use suggestions like "Add error handling to this function", and the mode commands "codebuff --lite" and "codebuff --max" are now listed explicitly. The layout also stops switching between a compact and expanded format based on terminal width, and a new note tells you that the assistant ignores your.gitignore and.codebuffignore files. You would notice the menu looking more consistent and informative the next time you start it.

ai.title: Simplify CLI help menu output
ai.summary: Replaces the detailed command-line usage section in `menu.ts` with a concise product description string. Removes imports of `cliArguments` and `cliOptions` from `cli-definitions.ts` within the menu module. Updates `--lite` and `--max` flags in `cli-definitions.ts` to `hidden: false`.

eli5.text: When you run the program without knowing what to type, the list of shortcuts it shows you got shorter and friendlier. Instead of printing every available option with its full description, it now shows a brief product description. The --lite and --max shortcuts, which were previously hidden from the menus, are now visible in the help output, so you can see and use them directly. Live today.

ai.title: CLI help simplification hides advanced options
ai.summary: New `cli-definitions.ts` centralizes CLI arguments and options, marking `--lite`, `--max`, `--experimental`, and `--model` as `hidden`. `index.ts` consumes these definitions to suppress hidden flags in `--help` output, while `menu.ts` renders a dedicated COMMAND-LINE USAGE section using `menuDescription` and `menuDetails` for visible flags. This reduces noise in standard help text while preserving access to advanced features via explicit flags.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant for help with how to use it from the command line, the simple, everyday options you might need are shown first, while the more advanced settings are tucked away so they don't clutter the main view. You can still access those advanced options by typing them in directly, they're just not advertised in the default help text. The list of available options and their explanations now live in one shared place so the help screen and the on-screen menu stay consistent with each other.

eli5.text: Your assistant just got a small housekeeping update that keeps everything running smoothly under the hood. The software bumped its internal version number to 1.0.284 and includes a batch of recent fixes: the assistant now starts new conversations with a correct record of past messages, handles file reading more reliably, responds more consistently when deciding when to stop, and organizes its notes about your project's files in a steadier, repeatable order. The on-screen menu has also been cleaned up so prompts show up in a clearer layout. You won't see a new feature, but the assistant should behave a little more predictably and load your project context with fewer glitches.

eli5.text: The team updated the system's self-checks so they expect the correct warning and informational text when a parameter or tool runs out of data unexpectedly. The parameter warning now also states that the missing end was added to the response, while the tool message was downgraded from a warning to informational and notes the stop sequence may have been omitted. Only internal test files changed; nothing live for users was affected.

ai.title: Add cli.userinputcomplete posthog event with latency
ai.summary: New AnalyticsEvent.USER_INPUT_COMPLETE ('cli.user_input_complete') added to common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts. npm-app/src/client.ts captures startTime before subscribeToResponse, tracks stepsCount and toolCallsCount across prompt-response chunks, and emits the event with userInputId, latencyMs, stepsCount, toolCallsCount on completion. Scope: shared core constants and CLI client. latencyMs measured as Date.now() delta from input capture to stream completion.

eli5.text: The app now quietly records how long it takes to finish answering each of your questions, sending that timing to their analytics along with a count of how many steps and tool calls the answer took. You won't see this data yourself, but it lets the team understand how fast responses complete from the moment your input is captured to when the stream ends. This applies to the shared core behavior and the command-line client, and the timing is measured as the difference between the current time captured before subscribing to the response and the time the stream completes.
